Initial access. m.alvarez opened Invoice_March_2024.docm and enabled macros; the macro loaded our DLL with rundll32. The mail gateway did not strip macro-enabled attachments from an external sender.
Basic host and network discovery from the first foothold. Every server answered net view, so there is no segmentation between the workstation VLAN and servers.
Keylogger left running in explorer.exe for 30 minutes. Nothing sensitive captured, but EDR never flagged the injection.

HalcyonTelemetryAgent runs as SYSTEM from a directory that standard users can write to. Swapping the binary gave us SYSTEM on WS-014. Fix the folder ACLs and audit other in-house services for the same mistake.
svc-helpdesk had an interactive session cached on a regular workstation. Its hash is valid on most servers. Credential Guard is not enabled.
Full ARP and port sweep of two /24s from WS-014. Expected an IDS alert here; the blue team confirmed none fired.
Scheduled task persistence on WS-014 (HalcyonUpdateCheck). Removed on day 3; see the cleanup comment.
Pass-the-hash with svc-helpdesk, then psexec to FS01. Service creation over ADMIN$ from a workstation should be a high-fidelity alert.
Finance share is readable by svc-helpdesk. Vendor payment spreadsheet pulled as proof of access.
Defender caught the second phishing payload on WS-022 within 20 minutes and blocked injection into explorer. Nice catch by the endpoint stack; we dropped this beacon.
SQL01 trusts Windows auth for svc-helpdesk with sysadmin rights. Customer billing data is reachable from here.
Domain admin adm.kowalski was logged into SQL01. Domain admins should only sign in to tier 0 systems. This is what led to full domain compromise.
DCSync of krbtgt, then a golden ticket for Administrator. Rotate the krbtgt password twice and review replication rights.
Production secrets sit in plaintext appsettings on WEB01. Move them into a secrets store.
Staged the finance share as a 48 MB zip and exfiltrated it over DNS TXT records across 25 minutes. Outbound DNS to arbitrary resolvers is allowed.
Day 3 was deliberately loud: a sweep plus psexec and winrm to five workstations in under an hour, to test whether the SOC notices. Check alert timing against these timestamps.
Persistence removed, beacons exited. Remaining artifacts: redteam_was_here.txt on WS-031 through WS-035.
